svg.title: Create the public root certificate — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Create the public root certificate
Practice CA server (TLS-CA01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.20
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-ca01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
cd ~/tls-ca
test ! -e root.crt && openssl req -new -x509 -sha256 -days 3650 -key root.key -out root.crt -subj
'/CN=SONIC Practice Root CA' -addext 'basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE,pathlen:1' -addext
'keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign'
openssl x509 -in root.crt -noout -subject -issuer -dates -fingerprint -sha256
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The subject and issuer both identify SONIC Practice Root CA. A SHA256 certificate fingerprint is
printed.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Paste the command. Enter the root key passphrase when asked.
2. The root certificate is public; the root key is not. The long validity here is a teaching choice, not
a DoD or enterprise policy.
3. This certificate is self-signed because a root is its own trust anchor. Self-signed does not mean
automatically trusted.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
